title: Tip 2 Tip
text:
The Long Way


Tip 2 Tip


1,000–1,200 KM 5 DAYS SELF-SUPPORTED




THE ORIGINAL


Start at The Hawk Beach, with the Atlantic behind you. Finish at Meat Cove, about 1,000–1,200 km of Nova Scotia later. What happens in between is largely up to you.


There is no prescribed route. Riders are given a series of checkpoints scattered across the province and choose how to connect them. The shortest route isn’t always the fastest, and the best idea at noon can look considerably worse at 2 a.m.


Ride solo or as a pair. Carry what you need. Find food, water and somewhere to sleep along the way. No support vehicles. No private supply drops. Just you, your bike, five days and a very long way north.


Tip 2 Tip grew from a few friends riding end-to-end in 2020 to its first race in 2021. Since then, each edition has taken riders on a different journey across Nova Scotia.


Race Rules FAQ

title: TIP 2 TIP!
text:
NOVA SCOTIA



750 KM 7,000+ M SOUTH → NORTH

title: TIP 2 TIP!
text:
The Route
This FKT is based on the honour system and GPS data. It follows a direct route from The Hawk Beach to the Meat Cove Campground sign. You can access the gpx file here.
All riders must travel south to north for this FKT.
The route is approximately 750 km. To account for GPS errors, a minimum distance of 747 km will be accepted. There is no cap on a longer route; however, it is in your best interest not to deviate too far from the original route.
Elevation: 7,000+ m
Previous attempts have recorded 7,270 m and 7,011 m of elevation gain. Differences are expected due to GPS error, construction detours, and resupply stops.

title: TIP 2 TIP!
text:
FKT Categories
There are two ways to attempt the Tip 2 Tip FKT: self-supported or supported.
There is a HUGE difference between the two. Whichever category you choose, you must follow it for the entire ride.
If you’re unclear about what counts as self-supported or supported, don’t hesitate to reach out with questions before your attempt.

Self-Supported
Do it all yourself!
There is no outside assistance. No support vehicles or people meeting you along the way. Get from A to B carrying your own gear and using services that are equally available to everyone.
No drafting behind another rider or vehicle.


Supported
A support vehicle and other outside assistance are allowed. Food, water, and supply drops are all OK.
You cannot draft behind the support vehicle or another rider.

title: TIP 2 TIP!
text:
Rules for an FKT Effort

Minimum distance is 747 km. Any detour must be the same length as, or longer than, the original route.
The ride must be recorded in full. Use a GPS device to record your route, distance, total time, and speed. Manually uploaded statistics are not accepted—you need a recording of your track. If you’re unsure whether your GPS device can be used, reach out before your attempt.
The clock never stops! Elapsed time is used for the FKT, not moving/ride time.
Resupply deviations are OK. Return to the route at the same point. If this isn’t possible because of construction or another closure, take a detour that is the same length as, or longer than, the original route.
Use the same bike for the entire ride.
Follow the rules of the road and respect other road users.
Wear a helmet at all times. Reflective clothing and equipment are highly recommended. You’ll be riding on busy highways for almost the entire route.

title: TIP 2 TIP!
text:
Safety
Every rider takes on risk when attempting this FKT. Be safe. Be smart.
Insurance through Cycling Nova Scotia is highly recommended in case an injury or accident occurs.
The Tip 2 Tip FKT is not a sanctioned event. It is an individual undertaking that can be attempted at any time of year and is open to anyone.

title: TIP 2 TIP!
text:
Planning an Attempt?
Please let the organizers of Tip 2 Tip NS know about your intention to ride at least two weeks before starting.
Take some photos, challenge yourself, and have fun!
The merch store is closed!

title: LOCOmotion 600
text:
The Long Way



600+ KM 60 HOURS SELF-SUPPORTED
The LOCOmotion 600 is a roughly 600+ km fixed-route, single-stage, self-supported endurance ride starting and finishing in Halifax, Nova Scotia.
LOCOmotion has become a bit of Nova Scotia cycling legend. Every year, riders make their way through rural towns and communities across the province with loaded bikes, tired legs and questionable amounts of convenience-store food, occasionally raising a few eyebrows along the way.
It’s challenging, but it’s also designed to be approachable. The LOCOmotion is a great introduction to self-supported endurance riding: long enough to test your legs, planning and resilience, while keeping you relatively close to civilization and the next place to find food, water or somewhere to sleep.
Ride it solo or as a pair. You have 2.5 days to get yourself around the route and back to Halifax.

title: LOCOmotion 600
text:
When?
June 12–14.
Registration for all races opens in January/February 2027.
Always be prepared. Nova Scotia’s coastal weather can turn cold, wet and windy, even in summer. Hypothermia is a risk at any time of year. Carry warm layers and waterproof gear, check the forecast, and be ready for changing conditions.




Past edition: LOCOmotion 2026. This is not the upcoming race course.


The Route
The LOCOmotion follows a fixed route of approximately 650 km, starting and finishing at the Halifax Citadel. Expect long days, changing weather, some gravel, a lot of Nova Scotia, and probably a few stories by the time you get back.
There are three checkpoints along the route. Checkpoint 2 is always volunteer-run and provides riders with a place to stop, rest and refuel.
Expect some gravel. 28 mm tires are considered the minimum width for this event. Having said that, your bike, your choice.
The route changes each year, is scouted each spring, and may undergo minor changes before the event.

title: LOCOmotion 600
text:
THINKING ABOUT RIDING?
You don’t need to have ridden hundreds of kilometres before, or even consider yourself an endurance cyclist, to take on LOCOmotion. Maybe this is your first big cycling challenge, maybe you’re curious about how far you can go, or maybe you’re an experienced ultra-racer looking to push the pace. Whatever brings you to the start line, LOCOmotion is about giving it a go, figuring things out along the way and seeing what you’re capable of.
There’s no single right way to approach the LOCOmotion. Some riders will race each other, some the clock. Others will take a more measured approach, stopping for a proper meal or a few hours of sleep. Whatever your strategy, the challenge is the same: get yourself and your bike back to Halifax as fast as you can.
There will be moments when you wonder why you signed up. Probably somewhere in the middle of the night, on a hill that really didn’t need to be there. But there will also be quiet roads at sunrise, unexpected kindness in small towns, conversations with other riders and the satisfaction of doing something you weren’t entirely sure you could do. And somehow by the end, the hardest parts have a way of becoming the fondest memories. You might arrive back in Halifax exhausted, but you’ll leave with stories, new friends and maybe even a reason to do it all again next year.

What does self-supported mean?
You’re responsible for getting yourself from start to finish.

No support cars, private water drops or outside assistance.
Riders must carry what they need or obtain it along the route.
Food, accommodation, supplies and other services must be commercially available to all riders.
No private assistance that isn’t equally available to another participant.

In short: you, your bike and whatever you can find along the way.

Registration

LOCOmotion 600 registration
Early bird — $75 Until April 3
Procrastination bird — $90 April 4–June 6
Registration fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.
Cost shouldn’t be the reason you can’t ride. If the registration cost is a barrier, contact tip2tipns@gmail.com.

GPS Tracking
Trackers are required for all riders.
Tracking is supplied and supported by Follow My Challenge USA.
You must register your own tracker or arrange a rental prior to the event. See the rider manual for detailed instructions.
If you have not registered or rented a tracker by the deadline, you will be removed from the rider list even if your LOCOmotion registration fee has already been paid.

Cycling Nova Scotia Membership
Riders must also have Cycling Nova Scotia coverage for the event.
Annual membership: $75 Single-event membership: $15 Already a current CNS member: $0
The membership provides insurance coverage for your ride.

Thinking about riding?
You don’t need to be a seasoned ultra-racer to line up for the LOCOmotion.
You do need to be prepared to look after yourself, keep moving when you’re tired, solve problems as they come up and spend a very long time on your bike.
That’s kind of the point.
Last-minute registration may be possible if space and trackers remain. Contact tip2tipns@gmail.com or reach out through Tip 2 Tip NS on Instagram or Facebook.

GENERAL RACE FORMAT
START: 06:00
FINISH: 18:00
LOCATION: Halifax Citadel look-off, harbour-facing
TIME LIMIT: 60 hours
FORMAT: Solo or pairs
DISTANCE: Approximately 650 km
STYLE: Self-supported

WHAT DOES SELF-SUPPORTED MEAN?
No support vehicles, private supply drops or personal crews waiting along the way. You’ll carry what you need, find food and water as you go, and decide when to stop, when to sleep and when to keep riding.
A rider manual containing checkpoints, final route information and all the nitty-gritty details will be sent to registered riders after the route has been scouted in the spring.

title: FAQ
text:
No support car. No water drops. No outside support - it’s all up to you to get to the finish!
In other words, all riders must be fully self-sufficient and not receive any private assistance. All food, lodging, etc. must be commercially available to all riders.




Only a SPOT tracker or Garmin InReach are supported by Follow My Challenge USA.




If you choose pairs, you need to finish with the person, or you’ll receive a DNF. You can still finish solo, but it won’t be counted. Pairs can share resources and draft, so if you start with those benefits and end as a solo rider, it’s not fair to those who were riding solo from the start.




Solo or pairs are the only two options. If you’re thinking of signing up with a few friends, it would be advised to all sign up as solo. You’d have to adhere to the rules of self-sufficiency (no drafting or sharing resources), but you’d be able to ride amongst one another.
When the ride takes off, you’ll notice packs start to form - people leapfrog one another and ride side-by-side at times. This is all OK and is a natural part of these events.




Yes! If it takes you longer to complete the routes, that’s no problem. Ride your own ride- it’s your adventure.
Organizers will not be at the finish after the cut-off.




This is entirely up to you and how you’re feeling. This is very much your own adventure, and we’d encourage you to sleep when needed. Safety is important! If you start seeing unicorns and dragons, and are nodding off while riding; seriously consider pulling over to rest.

The Long Way Cycling Series is Nova Scotia’s homegrown long-distance cycling series, born from a simple idea: why travel halfway around the world for an adventure when there’s plenty to be found right here?
It all started back in 2020, when international races were off the calendar and ultra-endurance cycling events in Atlantic Canada were pretty much nonexistent. Three cyclists, soon to become friends, had the same, slightly unhinged idea: ride across Nova Scotia, Tip 2 Tip! From The Hawk Beach to Meat Cove, roughly 750 km from one end of the province to the other, with plenty of hills, headwinds, and questionable life choices along the way.
And somewhere along the way, an idea took hold: if we wanted this kind of adventure here, surely other people did too? And so The Long Way Cycling Series was born, and is today a series of self-supported endurance cycling events that take riders across Nova Scotia and beyond. Different distances, different routes, different ways to get there, but the main idea is still the same: get on your bike, go somewhere, and see what happens along the way.

title: The Nor’Easter
text:
A NEW EASTBOUND CHALLENGE
The Nor’Easter, the next race in The Long Way series, is in development for 2028.
The concept is simple: start in Montreal, finish in Halifax, and manage yourself the whole way.
This page is an early teaser, not a full race manual. Distances, checkpoints, rules, and registration details are still being finalized.
More details coming as route planning continues. Follow us on Instagram for updates and announcements as we finalize the route and race details.

title: The Nor’Easter
text:
When?
Planned for 2028. Exact dates will be announced.
Registration for all races opens in January/February 2027.
Always be prepared. Nova Scotia’s coastal weather can turn cold, wet and windy, even in summer. Hypothermia is a risk at any time of year. Carry warm layers and waterproof gear, check the forecast, and be ready for changing conditions.

Race Rules FAQ

title: The Rules
text:
No debating the rules.
The Long Way Cycling Series events are self-supported rides. The rules are simple, and they’re based on the honour system. Please follow them and respect the self-supported nature of the event.

title: The Rules
text:
The Basics

Any pedal-powered bicycle is acceptable.
A helmet must be worn at all times while riding.
Follow the rules of the road.
No drafting, unless you are riding as a registered pair.
Anything you bring with you at the start must make it back to the finish with you, excluding consumables.

title: The Rules
text:
Riding as a Pair
Pairs may share resources and draft one another.
You must finish together. If one rider cannot finish, the pair will be recorded as a DNF.

title: The Rules
text:
Self-Supported Means Self-Supported

No outside assistance of any kind.
Any service you use—food, accommodation, mechanical services, supplies, etc.—must be commercially available to all riders.
Arranging to “meet” friends or family along the route is considered outside support.
Accommodation cannot be booked before the ride begins.

One exception: Because of the relative remoteness of the Cape Breton portion of the route, riders may book accommodation in advance for the night they expect to complete the ride.

title: The Rules
text:
Mechanical Problems
Mechanical problems happen.
If a mechanical issue cannot be resolved where it occurs, a rider may obtain a ride to access mechanical service. To continue the event, the rider must then be returned to the same location where they left the route and resume from there.

title: The Rules
text:
Be Seen
You need to be visible—especially at night.
Light-coloured and reflective clothing is strongly recommended. At night, you should light up like a Christmas tree.
Riders are required to carry:

Two rear lights: one flashing and one steady.
At least one front light capable of adequately illuminating the road at night.
At least one rear light must be running at all times while riding.
Ankle reflectors are highly recommended.

title: The Rules
text:
The Honour System
These rules are based on the honour system.
Please follow them, ride fairly, and uphold the self-supported nature of the Long Way Cycling Series.

title: The Hodge Podge
text:
Race Formats
There are two ways to take on The Hodge Podge. Go the full distance or share the adventure with a team.


THE FULL SERVE

Solo or pairs


Every kilometre. All yours.

Take on the entire Hodge Podge route from start to finish. Ride solo or as a pair, tackling every kilometre, climb, and whatever else Nova Scotia throws your way.


THE SHARING PLATE

Relay team


One route. Your team. Split the adventure.

Want to share the Hodge Podge? Gather a team and split the route however you like.
Riders can switch at designated checkpoints along the course. Take on one section, two, or as many as you want. There’s no set distance each rider needs to cover, but all rider changes must happen at official checkpoints. The active rider must reach the checkpoint before handing over to the next team member.
How you divide the distance is up to your team. Just make sure someone is always ready for the next serving!

title: Tip 2 Tip
text:
The Long Way



1,000–1,200 KM 5 DAYS SELF-SUPPORTED
Start at The Hawk Beach, with the Atlantic behind you. Finish at Meat Cove, about 1,000–1,200 km of Nova Scotia later. What happens in between is largely up to you.
Ride solo or as a pair. Carry what you need. Find food, water and somewhere to sleep along the way. No support vehicles. No private supply drops. Just you, your bike, five days and a very long way north.
Tip 2 Tip grew from a few friends riding end-to-end in 2020 to its first race in 2021. Since then, each edition has taken riders on a different journey across Nova Scotia.

title: Tip 2 Tip
text:
When?
August 28 – September 2, 2027.
Registration for all races opens in January/February 2027.
Always be prepared. Nova Scotia’s coastal weather can turn cold, wet and windy, even in summer. Hypothermia is a risk at any time of year. Carry warm layers and waterproof gear, check the forecast, and be ready for changing conditions.



Past edition: Tip 2 Tip 2025. This is not the upcoming race course.


The Route
There is no prescribed route. Riders are given a series of checkpoints scattered across the province and choose how to connect them. The shortest route isn’t always the fastest, and the best idea at noon can look considerably worse at 2 a.m.
Checkpoints change between editions; use the information provided for your race when planning your ride.
